title: Western Liang
capsule: Western Liang (西涼) was a short-lived state of the Sixteen Kingdoms period, founded in 400 CE by Li Gao, a Han Chinese administrator of the Jin dynasty, in the Dunhuang and Jiuquan region of the Hexi Corridor. The state controlled the western terminus of the Silk Road through Dunhuang, giving it strategic and commercial importance out of proportion to its small territory. Li Gao died in 417 and was succeeded by his sons, but the Northern Liang under Juqu Mengxun conquered the remaining territory in 421, eliminating the dynasty.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The political chronology is well recorded in the Zizhi Tongjian and Book of Jin; geographic extent is confined to the Hexi Corridor and is reasonably well bounded.
